stem: On a supine abdominal X-ray for suspected perforation, which statement is correct?

options.text: Free air under the diaphragm is the usual supine finding
The football sign can outline the falciform ligament
Abdominal X-ray is not used to assess for free gas
Dilated small bowel loops are a normal finding
A gasless abdomen is the expected normal appearance in older children

explanation: The football sign can outline the falciform ligament. It is a radiographic sign of free intraperitoneal gas on a supine abdominal X-ray.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because free air under the diaphragm is not the usual supine finding; free gas is better detected by other signs in this view
optionExplanations.B: Correct because the football sign can outline the falciform ligament, indicating free intraperitoneal gas
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because abdominal X-ray can be used to assess for free gas when perforation is suspected
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because dilated small bowel loops are an abnormal finding, not a normal one
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a gasless abdomen is not the expected normal appearance in older children

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
